feedback: Written before this candidate has raced, so no result is stated for it. Evidence so far: iteration 4 (0.14 m track, score 517.1) is the best design: oval 20/20, s-bend 6/20 (mean 519), slalom 0/20 with about 0.9 line-loss events per run. Iteration 1 (0.12 m, 482.7) and iteration 3 (0.10 m, 357.3) show that score rises with track width over that range. Iterations 2 and 3 lowered kp for narrower tracks and still lost score, so I have not scaled kp with track width in this package. Integration answers from evidence: (1) On the slalom, line loss is about 0.9 per run at 0.14 m and 1.0 at 0.12 m, so the wider track has not yet clearly raised it. (2) Oval steering_oscillation was 0.2255 at 0.14 m, 0.299 at 0.12 m and 0.252 at 0.10 m, so jitter did not rise with width. (3) Peak max_error is on bends, and the slalom's line loss occurs on the same bends, but the exact peak position is not resolved yet. (4) The outer sensors carry the largest weights (plus or minus 1.5), and no evidence yet shows they over-drive the signal. Next race: if s-bend finishes reach at least 6/20 and score is at or above 517, keep the wider track and consider 0.18 m only if slalom line_loss_events stay at or below 0.9. If the score falls below 517 with slalom line loss rising, the track is too wide for the sharpest bends, so return to 0.14 m and change sensing. Change one field at a time so the effect can be attributed.
requested_changes: If the 0.16 m race scores at or above 517 with slalom line_loss_events at or below 0.9: keep wheel_track at 0.16 m and try 0.18 m (the top of the allowed range) with all other fields unchanged. Evidence: iteration 4 at 0.14 m scored 517.1, above 482.7 at 0.12 m, so the monotonic trend has held over 0.10 to 0.14 m.

If the score falls below 517 or slalom line_loss_events rise above 0.9: return wheel_track to 0.14 m and change sensor_size from 0.016 to 0.012 m only. Evidence: slalom is 0/20 at every track width, with 0.9 to 1.0 line-loss events per run and progress near 0.2, so sensing is the next lever once track width stops helping.

If the 0.16 m race is near 517 with the s-bend unchanged: keep wheel_track at 0.14 m and narrow the sensor span to x = -0.05, -0.0333, -0.0167, 0, 0.0167, 0.0333, 0.05 m. Evidence: iteration 2 widened the span to 0.15 m together with a narrower track and mass change, and its s-bend fell to 0/20, so narrowing is the less risky direction to test.
